title: Stock Research with Claude
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext:
I've been enjoying using Claude for a lot of my investment research--great jumping off point. The one thing I wish it could do better was bring technical charts, live data, financial statements, etc. directly into a chat instead of me jumping from site to site to pull certain things.

I finally figured out to bring a lot of that into Claude (still working out a few things) and have really enjoyed the results so far. Hopefully, I'll be able to fully ditch the other websites soon. Sharing a quick demo of it so far

comments.author: csurkepulyka
comments.body: Just use BacktestLoop. It has an MCP that you can connect to Claude. it is way more accurate than this as it models the broker fees too

replies.author: SnowSilent7695
replies.body:
back tests are not really worth the paper they're written on--everybody claims they've back tested a strategy. 

Also, I've come across [https://backtestloop.com/](https://backtestloop.com/), and it's not it. Quite frankly, the data is incredibly noisy within that framework it's been [well-documented ](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-06/ai-bots-auditioning-for-wall-street-trading-are-mostly-losing?sref=iFWW0xUZ)that AI consistently lose money using that approach.

replies.author: csurkepulyka
replies.body:
BacktestLoop is using one of the best backtesting engines called Backtrader which is an open source package and has a long history of being trustworthy. Also BacktestLoop seems to have really good data too so in terms of backtesting I think it's a really good framework (I have been using it and no issues so far)

In terms of AI trading and AI losing money, yes that is true, but BacktestLoop is not an AI trading platform. It is a backtesting platform and among others it seems way more legit and more accurate unlike the other vibe coded apps that don't even have any contact details or any real company behind them (BacktestLoop is owned by a company called VectorSpell)

They support stocks, futures, forex and crypto up to 26 years of market data history down to the 1s timeframe (including multi timeframe support, training ML models, GPU support and so on)

I think their only real competitor is QuantConnect but they are slow and don't support Python at all (they support it through a weird .NET bridge called PythonNet that makes it extremely slow and not useable with Python strategies especially not with ML)

For quick iteration to test ideas I think BacktestLoop is nice. I just tested a Redditor's strategy that they claim to be profitable and it WAS profitable at least in the backtests.

Obviously backtests are just backtests, past performance won't predict the future. But in terms of backtesting, I think BacktestLoop is a really nice one and they have tons of integration (MCP, API etc)
